title: Silas and the Summit
premise: Gideon Whitlock, a storm chaser drowning in debt to the Meridian Syndicate, is given a dying prospector's map to the source of the Verrin River — a place the Syndicate has spent decades erasing from every record. Chased by Syndicate enforcers and shadowed by Wren, the prospector's estranged daughter who wants the map for herself, Gideon follows the river upstream through flooded canyons and abandoned mining towns, discovering that the 'forbidden source' is a geothermal anomaly the Syndicate has been secretly weaponizing. At the summit lake, Gideon must choose between selling the source's location to clear his debt or destroying it with Wren and the ragtag river folk who have become his family. He burns the map, collapses the access tunnel, and walks away owing nothing but his own name.
about_author: Noor Hartwell is a former river guide who spent six seasons on the waterways she now writes about, collecting stories from the people who live at their edges. She lives in a converted boathouse with an unreliable dog and an even more reliable canoe.

chapters.title: The Weight of Good Weather
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A storm-chasing run goes wrong when Syndicate collectors board his rig mid-tornado, cataloguing everything he owns against his debt. The chapter establishes his charm masking desperation, ending with him fleeing into the night with nothing but his compass.

chapters.title: A Trade in the Rain
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Sheltering under a rail bridge, he finds prospector Elias Marsh bleeding out, who trades a hand-drawn map for a promise: take it to the source, tell no one, burn it after. Elias dies as the Syndicate's searchlights sweep the valley.

chapters.title: What the Compass Points To
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Following the first leg upstream, Gideon realizes the compass doesn't point north — it points toward the river's headwaters, and it's been modified. First glimpse of a tail: a figure in oilskins tracking him along the far bank.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The tracker reveals herself: Elias Marsh's daughter, who learned of the map from her father's last letter and intends to claim what's hers. She disarms Gideon easily but can't read the map without him — an uneasy alliance forms over a fire neither trusts.

chapters.title: The Drowned Town
chapters.summary: Dual POV. They pass through Callow's Ford, half-submerged since the Syndicate dammed the lower river, meeting ferrywoman Odile and her adopted crew of displaced river kids — the first hint of a community the Syndicate ruined. Gideon feels something dangerously like belonging.

chapters.title: Paper Debts
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A Syndicate agent named Corvus catches up and makes an offer: deliver the map, wipe the debt clean, start over. Gideon lies and says he'll consider it, then can't sleep, staring at the compass and wondering what kind of man he's becoming.

chapters.title: Rapids and Reckonings
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A whitewater run nearly kills them both; Wren saves Gideon and admits her father chose a stranger over her, and she needs to know why. The emotional beat shifts from rivalry to reluctant partnership.

chapters.title: Odile's Bargain
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Returning to Odile's camp for supplies, they find Corvus there first, buying loyalty with promises of restored water rights. Odile plays both sides, warning Gideon privately: the Syndicate doesn't want the source found — it wants it kept.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Error
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Deciphering Elias's marginalia, Wren discovers the map shows two routes — one real, one bait designed to lead pursuers into a box canyon. Her father planned for betrayal; the question is whether he planned for her.

chapters.title: Box Canyon
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Corvus takes the bait route; rockslides seal his team in. Gideon, against Wren's objection, goes back to pull survivors out — including Corvus himself. Mercy becomes leverage when Corvus owes him now too.

chapters.title: High Water
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Spring melt floods the gorge, forcing them onto Odile's raft with her crew. Nights around the raft's cookfire knit Gideon into the group; he teaches the kids storm-reading, and for the first time in years stops calculating exits.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren finds Gideon's debt ledger and reads it aloud to the fire — not to shame him, but so the group understands exactly what the Syndicate holds over him. Instead of contempt, they offer to help pay it. Gideon refuses, ashamed, and rows off alone.

chapters.title: Corvus's Confession
chapters.summary: Corvus's POV. Alone in the canyon, Corvus reflects on thirty years serving men who erase towns, and on the chaser who pulled him out anyway. He sends a false report upstream, buying Gideon three days — knowing it ends his career either way.

chapters.title: The Staircase
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The river narrows into a vertical climb through abandoned mine shafts — Elias's old works. They find his camp, years of journals, and proof: the 'source' feeds a geothermal vent the Syndicate has been tapping to power something enormous and secret.

chapters.title: What Elias Knew
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Reading her father's final journal, Wren learns he wasn't prospecting — he was documenting, preparing to expose the Syndicate, and sent the map out because he knew he wouldn't survive. Her grief turns to purpose.

chapters.title: Summit Lake
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. They reach the source: a steaming caldera lake humming with tapped power, ringed by Syndicate infrastructure. Corvus arrives simultaneously, no longer an enemy but a witness. Below, Syndicate crews are already moving to intercept them.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The Syndicate's director arrives by helicopter and offers Gideon everything: debt erased, a new name, a share. All he must do is hand over the map and walk down the mountain alone. It's everything he wanted, and it costs him everyone he loves.

chapters.title: Burning the Map
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Gideon burns the map in front of the director — but the map was never the point; Elias's documentation, hidden in the compass casing, is. Wren triggers the floodgates Odile's crew rigged downstream, flooding the Syndicate's access tunnel.

chapters.title: Collapse
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The escape through the collapsing shafts, Corvus holding the door, the caldera venting harmlessly into open sky. Gideon nearly drowns in the surge and is dragged out by the river kids he taught to read water.

chapters.title: Downstream
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The descent, quiet and changed. Wren scatters her father's journals' copies to river towns so the truth travels faster than any Syndicate reprisal. She and Gideon finally speak plainly about Elias, forgiveness, and what comes next.

chapters.title: Settled Accounts
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Back at Callow's Ford, the Syndicate's power over the river broken, Gideon formally tears up his own ledger before Odile's crew. His debt dies with the map; his name, for the first time, belongs only to him.

chapters.title: Silas and the Summit
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, epilogue. We learn Silas was the compass's original owner — Elias's lost partner — whose name Gideon carved beside Wren's at the summit. Storm season returns; Gideon chases it again, but this time the raft behind him is full.
